children.name: Sylvia dohrni
children.description:
Dohrn's warbler (Sylvia dohrni), also known as Principe flycatcher-babbler, Dohrn's flycatcher, Dohrn's thrush-babbler, is a species of passerine bird in the family Sylviidae that is endemic to the island of Príncipe which lies off the west coast of Africa in the Gulf of Guinea.
Formerly placed within the genus Horizorhinus, it is now placed in the genus Sylvia based on the results of molecular phylogenetic studies. The specific name honours Heinrich Wolfgang Ludwig Dohrn.

children.name: Sylvia galinieri
children.description: The Abyssinian catbird (Sylvia galinieri), also known as the juniper babbler, is a small passerine in the family Sylviidae, endemic to the highland forests and scrub of Ethiopia.

children.name: Sylvia nigricapillus
children.description: The bush blackcap (Sylvia nigricapillus) is a species of bird in the family Sylviidae. It is endemic to South Africa and Eswatini. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist montane forests and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Sylvia atriceps
children.description:
The Rwenzori hill babbler (Sylvia atriceps) is a species of passerine bird in the family Sylviidae that is found in Africa.
The Rwenzori hill babbler was described by the English zoologist Richard Bowdler Sharpe in 1902 and given the binomial name Turdinus atriceps. The type locality is the Rwenzori Mountains on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The specific epithet atriceps is from the Latin ater for "black" and -ceps for "capped" or "headed". The Rwenzori hill babbler was formerly considered to be a conspecific with the African hill babbler. The species is monotypic.

children.name: Rhopophilus
children.description: The Chinese hill warblers — long-tailed, skulking birds of northern Chinese scrub and hillsides, with a complex, musical song. They were long considered babblers but molecular studies place them firmly within the sylviid radiation.

children.name: Rhopophilus pekinensis
children.description: The Beijing babbler (Rhopophilus pekinensis), also known as the white-browed Chinese warbler, Chinese hill warbler, or Chinese bush-dweller, is a species of bird in the genus Rhopophilus.

children.description: The Tarim babbler (Rhopophilus albosuperciliaris), also known as the Tarim hill warbler is a species of bird in the genus Rhopophilus.

children.name: Chrysomma
children.description: Yellow-eyed babblers — small, warm-brown birds of tall grasslands and reeds in South and Southeast Asia, with bright orange-yellow irises and a habit of creeping through dense stems like mice.

children.name: Chrysomma sinense
children.description:
The yellow-eyed babbler (Chrysomma sinense) is a passerine bird native to South and Southeast Asia. It inhabits shrubland, grassland and wetland habitats. On the IUCN Red List, it is listed as Least Concern because of its wide distribution and stable population.
Its common name refers to the traditional placement in the Old World babbler family Timaliidae although the genus Chrysomma forms a clade along with the parrotbills within the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Chrysomma altirostre
children.description:
Jerdon's babbler (Chrysomma altirostre) is a passerine bird native to wetlands and grasslands of the Indian sub-continent. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List since 1994. It is a member of the genus Chrysomma of the family Paradoxornithidae.
The common name commemorates the surgeon-naturalist Thomas C. Jerdon.

children.name: Fulvetta
children.description: Fulvettas — small, brownish babblers of Asian montane forests, formerly placed with the laughingthrushes but now recognised as sylviid warblers. They are active, gregarious foragers in the understorey and bamboo thickets.

children.name: Fulvetta cinereiceps
children.description:
The grey-hooded fulvetta (Fulvetta cinereiceps) is a bird species in the family Paradoxornithidae. Like the other typical fulvettas, it was long included in the Timaliidae genus Alcippe or in the Sylviidae.
Formerly, F. Cinereiceps was known as Manipur fulvetta, the birds properly referred to with this name have been split off and are now usually treated as a distinct species, F. Manipurensis. Another former subspecies of F. Cinereiceps that is nowadays usually considered distinct is the Taiwan fulvetta (F. Formosana).

children.name: Fulvetta formosana
children.description: The Taiwan fulvetta (Fulvetta formosana) is a species of bird in the family Sylviidae.

children.name: Fulvetta danisi

children.name: Fulvetta manipurensis

children.name: Fulvetta vinipectus
children.description:
The white-browed fulvetta (Fulvetta vinipectus) is a bird species in the family Paradoxornithidae. Like the other typical fulvettas, it was long included in the Timaliidae genus Alcippe or in the Sylviidae.
Ranging across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, it is endemic to Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.

children.name: Fulvetta ruficapilla
children.description: The spectacled fulvetta (Fulvetta ruficapilla) is a bird species in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Fulvetta ludlowi

Like the other typical fulvettas, it was long included in the Timaliidae genus Alcippe or in the Sylviidae. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, and Nepal.

children.name: Fulvetta claudi
children.description: A recently described fulvetta from the mountains of Yunnan in southwestern China, where it inhabits bamboo thickets in montane forest. It is grey-headed with warm brown upperparts.

children.name: Fulvetta sordidior
children.description: A dull-plumaged fulvetta of the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asian highlands, with a grey head, brown back, and darker throat.

children.name: Fulvetta przewalskii
children.description: A fulvetta from the mountains of western China, with a distinctive white throat and warm brown body. It is poorly known and occupies a restricted range.

children.name: Lioparus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Golden-breasted Fulvetta — a dazzling little bird of Asian montane bamboo forests with a brilliant golden-yellow breast and a complex, bubbling song.

children.name: Lioparus chrysotis
children.description: The golden-breasted fulvetta (Lioparus chrysotis) is a species of songbird found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Conostoma

children.name: Conostoma aemodium
children.description: The great parrotbill (Paradoxornis aemodius) is a bird species the Paradoxornithidae family.

children.name: Moupinia
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Rufous-tailed Babbler, a long-tailed, skulking bird of scrub and thickets in central China with a rich rufous tail and melodious song.

children.name: Moupinia poecilotis
children.description:
The rufous-tailed babbler (Moupinia poecilotis) is a bird species in the family Paradoxornithidae. As with many other species known as "babblers", it was formerly placed in the family Sylviidae. It is endemic to central China.
The genus Moupinia was introduced by the French ornithologists Armand David and Émile Oustalet in 1877.

children.name: Myzornis
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Fire-tailed Myzornis — one of the most spectacularly coloured birds in Asia, with vivid green, blue, yellow, black, and red plumage. It forages in mixed-species flocks in the mossy canopy of Himalayan cloud forests.

children.name: Myzornis pyrrhoura
children.description: The fire-tailed myzornis (Myzornis pyrrhoura) is a species of bird. Its genus Myzornis is monotypic, and has recently been placed in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Sinosuthora
